papers.title: Forest management, climate change, and roe deer: A conceptual model of how silvicultural systems shape habitat, population density, and browsing impacts
papers.authors: Sebastian Schwegmann, Max Kröschel, João Manuel Cordeiro Pereira, Andreea Petronela Spînu, Andreas Rigling
papers.abstract: Management of roe deer in European forests may be challenging due to their impact on tree regeneration and potential negative effects on tree species composition, forest resilience and various ecosystem services including timber production. However, silvicultural practices themselves are key drivers in shaping roe deer habitat and consequently affecting deer population densities and the browsing susceptibility of young trees. Silvicultural interventions shape forest structures such as canopy closure, and thus the light availability and thermal cover at the forest floor. Light availability on the forest floor in turn determines vegetation growth and therefore forage availability and quality, as well as hiding opportunities for roe deer. Additionally, natural disturbances such as bark beetle outbreaks increasingly affect European forests at different spatial scales, influencing the interactions between roe deer and forests, while also underscoring the need for increased forest resilience amid climate change. This review provides an overview of the observed and potential impacts of silviculture and climate change–related disturbances on deer population density and browsing. It systema

papers.title: Impacts of needle-leaved forests landscape pattern and environmental factors on the spatial differentiation of pine wilt disease in China
papers.authors: Yimeng Lv, Jixia Huang, Shixiang Zong, Tong Yang, Chong Zhao
papers.abstract: Following its emergence in China, pine wilt disease (PWD) has continuously expanded, creating substantial risks to regional forest ecosystems. However, most existing research emphasizes climate and other macro-scale associated factors, and lacks long-term and systematic analysis approached through the lens of forest landscape patterns. The research focuses on describing the spatiotemporal dynamics of PWD in China across the period 1982–2020 and identifying the dominant factors influencing its distribution. We specifically examined how needle-leaved forest landscape patterns interact with environmental conditions to shape the spread of PWD across regions. We applied the optimal parameters-based geographical detector (OPGD) model to analyze the spatial differentiation of PWD outbreaks. Needle-leaved forest landscape metrics and environmental variables were integrated to evaluate their individual and combined effects on disease spread. PWD has progressively expanded over the past four decades. The epidemic was primarily distributed along the southeastern coastal zones and subsequently extended toward the northwestern interior. papers.title: The Curse of Black Sigatoka: A Backward Bifurcation Perspective
papers.authors: Bernard Asamoah Afful, Luis F. Gordillo
papers.abstract: Abstract Black Sigatoka disease (BSD), also known as black leaf streak disease, is an airborne fungal infection caused by Pseudocercospora fijiensis that severely impacts global banana and plantain production. Its persistence and resistance to eradication make it one of the most challenging plant diseases to manage. In this paper, we propose a deterministic pathogen-host model to describe BSD dynamics. Due to dual transmission pathways (ascospores and conidia) and mate limitation in sexual reproduction, the model exhibits a backward bifurcation: a stable endemic equilibrium coexists with the disease-free equilibrium for certain parameter values in which the basic reproduction number, $$\mathcal {R}_0$$ R 0 , is less than 1. This phenomenon explains why control strategies that solely reduce $$\mathcal {R}_0$$ R 0 below one may fail. For the backward bifurcation regime, we perform sensitivity analysis of the endemic equilibrium using normalized forward sensitivity indices, Latin Hypercube Sampling, and Partial Rank Correlation Coefficients. papers.title: Sources, Transmission, and Control of Salmonella in Vertically Integrated Broiler Chicken Production: Farm, Hatchery, and Processing Plant
papers.authors: Deepak Subedi, Bharath Mallavarapu, Pranita Patil, Abhisek Niraula, Milan Kandel
papers.source: OpenAlex / Comprehensive Reviews in Food Science and Food Safety
papers.abstract: Salmonella remains one of the most important foodborne pathogens associated with poultry products, despite substantial progress in processing hygiene and antimicrobial interventions. This review critically examines the sources, transmission routes, and control strategies for Salmonella in vertically integrated broiler production systems. Attention is given to contamination originating from breeder flocks, hatcheries, feed, water, litter, grow-out farms, transport, processing environments, and finished products. Preharvest interventions, including biosecurity, breeder and hatchery control, vaccination, litter and water management, feed hygiene, probiotics, prebiotics, organic acids, essential oils, bacteriophages, and bacteriocins, are evaluated according to mechanism, evidence strength, and commercial relevance. Postharvest interventions, including scalding, picking, evisceration control, chilling, peroxyacetic acid application, carcass rinses, post-chill treatments, and finished-product verification, are reviewed in relation to microbial reduction and process control. papers.title: A Review of Machine Learning in Species Distribution Modeling under Climate Change in West Africa
papers.authors: Dr Muhammad Kabir Usman, Nana Hauwa Aliyu, Ameer Abdulaleem, Seidu Mohammed, Babalola Jamiu Babatunde
papers.source: OpenAlex / Asian Journal of Geographical Research
papers.abstract: Species distribution modelling (SDM) has become a central instrument for anticipating how biodiversity is redistributed under climate change, and machine learning now supplies most of the algorithmic capacity behind these predictions. West Africa combines high climatic exposure, dense reliance on wild biological resources, and thin biodiversity records, so the region is a demanding setting in which the strengths and weaknesses of machine learning SDMs are exposed. Scope. Peer-reviewed studies published between 2020 and 2026 were synthesised to describe how correlative SDMs, tree-based ensembles, and deep learning have been applied to West African flora, fauna, disease vectors, and agricultural pests, and to assess the treatment of data quality, model transferability, and reporting standards. Key findings. Maximum entropy modelling remains the dominant approach, yet tree-based ensembles and, more recently, deep neural networks are being adopted where occurrence volume permits. papers.title: Development of research on retention forestry over the last four decades
papers.authors: Lena Gustafsson
papers.abstract: Four decades ago, a modified form of forest management was introduced with the aim of reconciling wood production and environmental values. Central is the deliberate retention at harvest of structural components key to biodiversity and ecological processes such as old trees, dead trees and specific tree species. This “retention forestry” model was initially implemented in clearcutting forestry but has later been introduced also in continuous-cover forestry and is today widespread on different continents. This review describes and analyses scientific publications on retention forestry in boreal and temperate regions with a focus on biodiversity, a key aspect of the model, based on a systematic literature search. The expansion of the practical application of the model in different parts of the world is described, as well as large-scale experiments. The use of terms associated with retention forestry (green-tree retention”, “variable retention”, “microhabitat”, “lifeboating”, “biological legacy”) regionally and over time is described. papers.title: Prevention of Destructive Fishing in the Waters of Tual City: Effective Surveillance and Law Enforcement Strategies
papers.authors: Suharta ., Sigit Bintoro, Riyan Maulana, Ismi Isti Anah
papers.source: Crossref / International Journal of Multidisciplinary Research and Growth Evaluation
papers.abstract: <jats:p>Destructive fishing in the waters of Tual City remains a significant environmental and socio-economic issue, threatening marine biodiversity and the livelihoods of local fishermen. This study analyzes the problem using a SWOT approach, identifying strengths such as existing government regulations and rich marine resources, weaknesses including limited enforcement capacity and economic dependence on harmful fishing practices, opportunities such as growing global demand for sustainable seafood, and threats like illegal fishing and climate change. Based on the SWOT analysis, several policy recommendations are proposed, including strengthening law enforcement, promoting sustainable alternative livelihoods, enhancing education and awareness programs, expanding marine protected areas (MPAs), and creating market incentives for responsible fisheries. These strategies aim to transition Tual City towards sustainable fisheries management, balancing environmental conservation with economic development. Effective implementation of these policies will not only mitigate destructive fishing but also ensure long-term resilience for both the ecosystem and local fishing communities.</jats:p>

Context The large pine weevil ( Hylobius abietis L.) is a major bark-feeding pest of conifer seedlings in Europe. Aims We investigated how pine weevil feeding affects organ-specific compounds from primary and secondary metabolism in Scots pine ( Pinus sylvestris L.) seedlings and whether these responses differed between two local provenances. Methods Soluble sugars were quantified in roots and needles to assess organ-specific changes in carbohydrate status. Phenolic compounds and non-volatile metabolomic profiles were analyzed in needles to evaluate systemic chemical responses after seven days of pine weevil feeding. Alerts are subsequently assessed by infection prevention and control (IPC) experts to determine their epidemiological relevance. This study compares expert assessment of CLAR alerts with genotyping results. DESIGN: Retrospective observational study. METHODS: We analyzed all CLAR alerts and genotyping reports generated during routine IPC activities between 08/2019 and 12/2024. CLAR alerts were classified relevant/not relevant based on epidemiological assessment by IPC physicians. Selected isolates were genotyped when transmission was suspected. Where multiple alerts and genotyping reports were available for an epidemiological cluster, only the first alert with genotyped isolates and the first corresponding genotyping report were considered, in order to emulate conditions at the onset of potential outbreaks. papers.title: Evidence boundaries and integrated disease management of microbial disease risks in protected Cymbidium faberi production: a translational framework and validation agenda
papers.authors: Yufeng Deng, Dongfeng Wei, Shichao Gu, Min Yu, Jinzhi Yao
papers.abstract: Cymbidium faberi ( C. faberi ) is an economically and culturally important orchid in East Asia, yet direct species-specific evidence for microbial diseases under protected cultivation remains limited. This critical narrative review synthesizes evidence on orchid diseases, protected-crop disease ecology, plant pathogen detection and diagnosis, biological control, and plant microbiome interactions. Direct C. faberi studies comprise one localized anthracnose-oriented report, baseline studies of root- and rhizosphere-associated microorganisms, and candidate antagonistic endophytes. However, they do not establish a contemporary pathogen inventory, species-resolved epidemiology, disease-associated microbiome dynamics, or validated management efficacy. Evidence from related Cymbidium species, other orchids, protected crops, and general plant-pathology systems is therefore interpreted according to host proximity, pathogen biology, production environment, and management relevance. papers.abstract: <jats:p>Background: Minimally invasive coronary artery bypass grafting (MICS CABG) via left anterior thoracotomy has emerged as a less invasive alternative to conventional open sternotomy (OPEN CABG), offering potential benefits in perioperative outcomes and complication rates. Objective. The aim of this study was to compare procedural characteristics, ventilation duration, drainage volumes, and postoperative complications between MICS CABG and OPEN CABG in a single-center cohort in Bosnia and Herzegovina. Methods. This retrospective cross-sectional study included 262 patients who underwent surgical revascularization between January 2019 and June 2023. Results. MICS CABG was associated with a shorter median procedure time (2.5 vs. 3.5 hours, p<0.001) and reduced mechanical ventilation duration (11.0 vs. 14.0 hours, p<0.001). Although ICU stay was similar (3.0 days, p=0.001), total hospitalization was shorter for MICS CABG (6.0 vs. 7.0 days, p<0.001). papers.abstract: This study brings out a new AI-based smart irrigation device aimed at solving the increasing problem of water shortage and poor agricultural procedures using emulated edge-based controllers. This combination of environmental sensing, lightweight machine learning algorithms and actuation on microcontrollers enables the system to do real time, adaptive irrigation scheduling. Their implementation of important parts like Raspberry Pi 4 as an AI inference module and an STM32 microcontroller as an actuator controller accelerates the responsiveness, increases security, and saves energy consumption since there is no need in cloud computing. Using the local climatic and soil moisture data the machine learning model identifies optimum irrigation time and duration looking at various parameters such as temperature, humidity, rain and crop-specific thresholds. The whole decision-making process is automated and carried out at the edge that makes it functional even without interruption in areas with poor or no internet connection. papers.title: Opinion Dynamics Modelling: Distinct Attraction and Repulsion Topologies Highlight Quantitative Effects of Trolling
papers.authors: Jake Boyce, Matteo Farina, Jody C. McKerral, Sergiy Shelyag, Mathew L. Zuparic
papers.abstract: Abstract We introduce a model of opinion dynamics based on networked nonlinear differential equations. The model combines a linear attraction with a repulsive hyperbolic tangent interaction, labelled controversialness . For low controversialness, the model displays universal consensus, which is typical of opinion models. As controversialness increases, opinion behaviours such as polarisation , clustering , and dissensus emerge, dependent on the network topology. By placing attractive and repulsive interactions on distinct networks, this model is able to simulate the manipulative effects of trolls by introducing controversy, which may be associated with mis/disinformation, toxic messaging, and encouraging provocative questioning and/or emotional posting. This work offers an analytical and statistical analysis of model results, under a wide variety of topologies and initial conditions, while also generalising cluster detection algorithms typically applied to discrete models.

papers.title: Integrated differential transcript usage and transcript abundance analyses reveal isoform-level remodeling in clear cell renal cell carcinoma
papers.authors: Chinaza F. Nnam, Yiping Li, Minghui Zhang, Erick Alexander Mboya, Fred Kolling
papers.abstract: Clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) is characterized by transcriptional reprogramming driven by hypoxia signaling, metabolic rewiring, and immune modulation. While gene-level analyses have defined key features of ccRCC biology, they do not capture isoform-level variation arising from alternative splicing. Differential transcript usage (DTU) represents an additional regulatory layer that may influence protein function, pathway activity, and clinical outcomes, yet its role in ccRCC biology and prognosis remains incompletely understood. We assessed differential expression in 127 ccRCC tumors and 33 normal-adjacent tissues from the Dartmouth Cancer Center cohort, with external validation in 94 CPTAC tumors, adjusting for cell-type proportions. Formal DTU was first tested using DRIMSeq/stageR, which evaluates shifts in relative isoform proportions within genes. StageR-significant transcripts were then evaluated in a separate covariate-adjusted limma-voom transcript-abundance analysis incorporating clinical and tumor microenvironment covariates. papers.abstract: This participatory action research, employing a cross-sectional quantitative survey combined with qualitative methods, aimed to (1) assess the health impacts of the Lam Takong Wind Power Project (Phase 2) using the six-step Health Impact Assessment (HIA) framework, (2) analyze the social determinants of health (SDH) in the project-area community, and (3) develop participatory recommendations to prevent and mitigate health impacts. Qualitative data were collected from 30 purposively selected key informants. papers.title: AgroGuard AI: A Trustworthy Adaptive Architecture for Crop Disease Intelligence under Environmental Non-Stationarity
papers.authors: Lanre Adams, Timothy Okoliko, Jennifer Okoliko
papers.source: OpenAlex / International Journal of Modern Science and Research Technology
papers.abstract: Deep learning systems for crop disease recognition are routinely reported at above 95% accuracy on curated benchmarks, yet their field performance degrades sharply and silently once deployed. The cause is not a modelling deficiency in the conventional sense but a violation of the stationarity assumption on which supervised learning rests: the agro-climatic environment that generates the data is itself non-stationary. Humidity regimes shift between seasons, pathogen populations evolve, cultivar mixes change, sensor hardware ages, and the relationship between visual symptom and disease label drifts with them. A model frozen at training time therefore decays monotonically, and — more damagingly for trust — it decays while continuing to report high confidence. This manuscript presents AgroGuard AI, a five-layer reference architecture that treats environmental non-stationarity as a first-class design constraint rather than a deployment nuisance. The architecture couples four mechanisms that are usually studied in isolation. papers.title: Invasive or non-invasive trapping of otters and the use of scent lures and baits: a review
papers.authors: Lea Maria Schiebe, Frank Rosell, Hanna Kavli Lodberg-Holm
papers.source: OpenAlex / European Journal of Wildlife Research
papers.abstract: Abstract Animals are often trapped to learn more about a species’ behavioural ecology, either invasively with live traps or non-invasively with hair- or camera traps. The use of scent lures or baits can help to attract animals to the trap site. The aim of this study was to identify the best and most efficient trapping techniques and scent lure or bait for research on Eurasian otters ( Lutra lutra ). The systematic literature review, in accordance with PRISMA guidelines, was designed to include results for all otter species. It recovered 16 papers, most published between 2011 and 2020 covering six otter species. This review identified six different main trapping methods (net traps, leghold traps, cage traps as live- or hair traps, suitcase traps, hair traps using sticks, and camera traps). Scent lures were only utilized in the hair- and camera trapping studies. Due to the limited comparability of the studies, the most effective trapping or scent lure/bait method could not be concluded. The review therefore provides the pros and cons of these various capture techniques for otter research. papers.title: Competition and soil conditions limit the growth of High Arctic non‐native plants
papers.authors: Jana Ruethers, L. Bakker, Sebastian Döetterl, Simone Fior, Cara Magnabosco
papers.abstract: Non-native vascular plant species in the High Arctic are currently restricted mainly to settlements and other anthropogenically disturbed areas. The reasons for this remain unclear, but climate or dispersal do not appear to be the main limiting factors. Instead, biotic interactions combined with soil conditions may play key roles. As the High Arctic becomes warmer and human activity increases, identifying the factors that currently limit non-native plant establishment in tundra ecosystems will be important for managing invasions. To address this, we conducted a growth experiment with three non-native vascular plant species from the archipelago of Svalbard, manipulating temperature, nitrogen availability, competition with four native vascular plant species, and simulated stages of soil development. In response, a wide range of machine learning (ML) techniques have been explored for effective disease detection and classification. This systematic review provides a comprehensive analysis of 102 peer-reviewed studies published between 2001 and 2024, exclusively focused on ML-based approaches for identifying plant leaf diseases. Based on the PRISMA methodology, studies were selected from four major databases and organized under eight research questions (RQs), covering the end-to-end ML pipeline. The review investigates key components such as dataset collection methods, model architectures, evaluation strategies, and comparative model performance. It further analyzes the distribution of studies by plant type, disease category, and publication source. Halophytes host a diverse community of endophytic fungi that are naturally adapted to extreme saline and arid environments. These fungi establish symbiotic associations with their host plants, improving plant performance and contributing to ecosystem services, thereby making them valuable for sustainable agriculture and environmental management. In agricultural systems, these endophytes promote plant growth and yield by producing phytohormones, solubilizing nutrients, and activating stress-protective pathways. They further enhance tolerance to salinity and drought by maintaining ion homeostasis and stimulating antioxidant defence mechanisms. papers.abstract: Peru is one of the countries with the greatest diversity of native chili peppers, which make a significant contribution to the highly valued gastronomy of this nation. However, the use of these chili peppers remains localized, resulting in a limited number of studies focused on these species, which restricts their industrial utilization and increases the risk of extinction. For this reason, this review addresses topics ranging from their geographical distribution and genetic resources (encompassing national collections such as INIA with 712 accessions within a global germplasm context including the WVC with 8,264 accessions) to their industrial applications, including morphological characteristics, sensory profiles, and chemical composition. It was observed that native Peruvian chili peppers have the potential to be used in the development of pharmaceutical, cosmetic, and food products, due to their content of compounds with biological activity such as capsaicinoids, carotenoids, phenolic compounds, vitamins, and minerals; they also present a wide range of pungency levels according to the Scoville scale. papers.authors: Antonella Zarra
papers.source: OpenAlex / EUR Research Repository (Erasmus University Rotterdam)
papers.abstract: When should institutions step in and regulate novel technologies such as AI? Traditionally, scholars involved in the economic analysis of law would answer along the following lines: “when the benefits of regulation outweigh the costs.”24 This thesis examines the contributions of law and economics to addressing AI governance challenges by analyzing market failures, liability allocations, and the effectiveness of regulatory interventions in order to answer two research questions: How should AI rules be designed? Are standard regulatory tools sufficient? To accomplish this, the present thesis explores the extent to which existing legal frameworks can internalize (and mitigate) AI-related risks and how economic, design thinking, and behavioral principles can inform regulatory design in an effort to ensure optimal policy outcomes.

The T4 bacteriophage, a mindless nanoscale machine whose structure executes functions that map onto both empowering and disempowering strategies in Forde's framework of social dynamics, demonstrates this principle at the nanoscale. The strategies mapped include security, knowledge, hope, fairness, unity, and dignity, alongside their darker counterparts: nativism, hierarchy, misinformation, subjugation, dehumanization, and fear.
